app.title: Climate Change in Graphs
app.summary: A person picks a topic from a home page of buttons: emissions, energy, ice, maps, ocean, physical quantities or temperature. On each topic page they narrow the time axis with a year-range slider or typed bounds. They then use dropdowns to choose which chart, dataset, region, season or variable to show, and pick countries to overlay. Charts set several records or scenarios against each other, with uncertainty bands, moving averages and fitted trendlines that show slope and p-value on hover. Map pages show the spatial pattern of a trend or projection for a chosen period, with hatching where the trend is not significant.

task.text: Browse published climate indicator records and projections by topic, narrowing time ranges and choosing which series, regions and scenarios to compare.

data.text: Many published global and regional indicator records: annual and monthly time series with uncertainty, scenario pathways to 2100, per-country tables, and gridded maps of trends and projections. Each is fetched from its source URL, with a bundled file as fallback.
data.item: one indicator series from one dataset, such as an annual anomaly record, a country's yearly emissions or a gridded trend map

stage.text: exploring and comparing published indicator records and projections, after the source data is published

mechanism.text: A home page of topic buttons leads to pages of stacked charts. On each chart, a year-range slider sets the x-axis, and a dropdown or multiselect chooses which series, countries, season or period are drawn. Hover shows values and, for trendlines, the fitted slope and p-value; map sections swap between precomputed gridded fields chosen from a dropdown.

field.text: climate indicator time series, trend fitting and gridded model projections in climate science

workflow.name: browse a collection of indicator charts by topic, narrowing time and choosing series

steps.here: each loader fetches a published record from its source URL, falls back to a bundled file if the request fails, and caches the result

steps.step: choose a topic to look at
steps.here: the home page shows seven buttons (Emissions, Energy, Ice, Maps, Ocean, Quantities, Temperature), and each one switches to its page

steps.step: narrow to a period of interest
steps.here: a year-range slider above each chart sets the x-axis range; on the temperature page, number boxes either side of the slider let the person type the bounds

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: dropdowns pick the chart, dataset, hemisphere, season or variable, and a multiselect chooses which countries to overlay
the chart overlays four temperature records, several countries or several policy pathways with their ranges; sector charts are split into one small panel per region

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: the app computes moving averages, seasonal means (leaving out seasons with missing months) and a linear trendline whose slope and p-value show on hover

steps.step: see where on the globe it happens
steps.here: choropleths by country, and Mollweide contour maps of trend or projected change for a chosen period, with hatching where the trend is not significant or the models disagree

distinctive: every remote source has a bundled backup file, so the charts still draw when a data provider is offline
the same quantity from several independent records is re-baselined to a common reference period, so the records can be overlaid
trendlines report their slope equation and a regression p-value in the hover text
maps hatch cells where the trend is not statistically significant or model agreement is low
past records run on into scenario pathways to 2100, each labelled with its projected end-of-century warming
